explanation: One of Jacob's sons, known for his ability to interpret dreams and his righteousness.
An Egyptian officer who bought Joseph as a slave and put him in charge of his household.
The woman who tried to seduce Joseph but was rejected by him.
Potiphar's wife accused Joseph of attempting to rape her after he rejected her advances.
The place where Joseph was sent after being falsely accused by Potiphar's wife.
The ability to interpret dreams, which Joseph was known for having.
Joseph was entrusted with great responsibility both in Potiphar's house and later in prison.
Joseph's moral principles and honesty, which led him to reject Potiphar's wife's advances.
God was with Joseph throughout all his trials and gave him success and progress.
